candidates.title: Conditional settlement with composable evidence requirements
candidates.behavioral_need: A destination accepts a submitted obligation, but asset settlement waits until its signed combination of additional signatures, recipient acceptance, documents, proofs or other conditions is satisfied. Funded escrow is an optional specialization.
open_theory_choices: Predicate algebra versus staged protocol types; conjunction, alternatives and thresholds; who may supply evidence; monotone evidence versus revocation.
Commit document content/version and issuer authority; distinguish possession of bytes from certification of real-world truth.
Proof relation binds obligation identity, terms, evidence commitments, predecessor/history and allowed effects/bounds to ZKIRv3 execution.
adversarial_scenarios: Recipient signs different terms after submission.
Valid proof is replayed from another obligation.
One attestation is counted twice in a threshold.
Document is replaced at the same URL.
An issuer revokes evidence before a signed settlement cut-off.

future_research.PL_theory: Compare semantic accounts and prove the selected safety properties; no novelty or theorem claim yet.

future_research.deployed_languages: Require pinned implementation and deployment evidence separately; names and analogies alone are insufficient.

candidates.product_constraint: Permissionless language for all Midnight DeFi developers; real compilation to pinned ZKIRv3; proof-carrying signed formal intention. No project admission registry.

candidates.title: Durable partial obligations and single-use settlement rights
candidates.behavioral_need: Keep pending obligation, funding, evidence and residual rights identifiable across multiple submissions; executing admission must not imply discharging settlement.
open_theory_choices: Separate signed-intent nonce, obligation identity, stage identity, fill identity and settlement-consumption marker.
Persistent linear/affine rights versus state-machine predicates; fund locks versus unreserved commitments.
Stage-specific deadlines and revocation policy; obligations already admitted may survive expiry of admission authorization.
adversarial_scenarios: Two concurrent continuations spend the same funded right.
Cancellation races with final evidence.
Fresh intent replays an old continuation.
Admission deadline expires before recipient acceptance.
Upgraded code preserves account name but changes the signed meaning.

candidates.title: Evidence-scoped knowledge and residual recovery duties
candidates.behavioral_need: Represent known local failures, pending work, unknown external consequences and confirmed outcomes separately; keep recovery duties when remote effects are not established.
open_theory_choices: Epistemic state with evidence provenance versus a finite phase/error algebra.
Receipt-local compensation versus global rollback; explicit reliable external nonexecution certificates.
Dimensionally separate assets, liabilities and permission capabilities; relate them through typed predicates, not addition.
adversarial_scenarios: Transfer-call fails after recipient received assets.
Malformed successful callback result.
Timeout despite reliable proof of nonexecution.
Maker paid but taker payout fails.
Duplicate callback attempts to create a second refund.

candidates.title: Partial fills preserve proportional rights and fees
candidates.behavioral_need: Support explicit divisible obligations while preserving remaining quantities, bounds, fee policy and termination behavior.
open_theory_choices: Partial fill as opt-in quantitative refinement versus independently signed sub-obligations.
Per-fill versus aggregate fee and rounding constraints; price threshold before or after fees.
Fairness/liveness assumptions and residual dust policy.
adversarial_scenarios: Splitting into many tiny fills amplifies rounded fees.
Fill exceeds remaining amount.
A net maker price violates a pre-fee quoted floor.
Zero-output rounding consumes a right.
Partial fill races with close.

candidates.title: Permissionless programs with scoped application authority
candidates.behavioral_need: Any Midnight DeFi developer may write and compile supported programs, while signed applications may choose counterparties, recipients, attesters and acceptable proof verifiers.
open_theory_choices: Capability scope and delegation proof rules; proof-verifier identity binding; local counterparty policy versus platform gate.
Versioned semantics and verifier-key evolution without silently reinterpreting existing signed obligations.
adversarial_scenarios: Untrusted relayer forges the forwarded signer.
Compiler platform requires project registration despite valid program/proof.
Valid app-specific recipient restriction is incorrectly removed in the name of permissionlessness.
Governance replaces verifier code under a persistent address.

candidates.title: Simulation reports and proofs identify their semantic scope
candidates.behavioral_need: Differentiate local simulated validity, proven admitted transition and evidence of eventual external settlement.
open_theory_choices: Effect abstraction and assume-guarantee contracts for callbacks.
Proof claims indexed by state root, program version, environment assumptions and external-effect frontier.
adversarial_scenarios: A cached AuthCall succeeds while recipient rejects.
Fee or nonce state changes after simulation.
An event is indexed from a failed execution receipt.
Locally verified ZK proof is displayed as completed remote payment.
